papers.title: The Mediterranean Diet vs. 21st Century Lifestyle: A Review
papers.abstract: The Mediterranean diet (MD) is widely recognized for its health benefits and its association with reduced incidence of noncommunicable diseases. However, modern lifestyles, characterized by increased consumption of ready-to-eat (RTE) foods and limited time for meal preparation, pose significant barriers to maintaining a healthy diet. Although numerous reviews have explored the nutritional benefits of the MD, fewer studies have examined how contemporary lifestyles conflict with dietary and behavioral habits of the Mediterranean lifestyle, and how food systems can adapt to MD principles. Therefore, this review examines the challenges of maintaining the MD in the context of 21st-century urban living and explores practical strategies for its integration into contemporary dietary patterns. The main characteristics and health-promoting components of the MD and Mediterranean lifestyle are reviewed, considering how changes in dietary habits, physical activity, social interactions, and the food environment influence adherence. The review also discusses interventions to promote MD adherence and the potential of RTE foods incorporating Mediterranean ingredients to offer convenient, nutritionally improved alternatives. Additionally, the valorization of Mediterranean agri-food by-products is discussed as an opportunity to incorporate bioactive compounds and functional ingredients into food products.

papers.title: User Acceptance and Interaction Design for AR Guides at Industrial Heritage Sites: Integrating Cultural Identity into a TTF–TAM Framework with Eye-Tracking Evidence
papers.abstract: Smart guide systems for industrial heritage sites must support spatial navigation, information access, and understanding of heritage content. However, translating user acceptance findings into decisions about visual content, information hierarchy, and interface interaction remains challenging. This study incorporates cultural identity, defined as visitors’ identification with industrial symbols, historical narratives, and cultural values, into an integrated task–technology fit (TTF) and technology acceptance model (TAM) framework. Structural equation modeling of 295 valid questionnaire responses examines factors associated with behavioral intention to use smart guide systems. Cultural identity is significantly and positively associated with perceived usefulness and behavioral intention. Task–technology fit, perceived ease of use, and perceived usefulness are also significantly and positively associated with behavioral intention. Complementary eye-tracking experiments and semi-structured interviews in the context of Wuhan Iron and Steel Group’s industrial heritage examine visual attention and participants’ understanding of heritage content. Fixation heatmaps, scanpaths, and area-of-interest metrics characterize attention patterns, while interviews explore how participants interpret industrial history and cultural meanings. Descriptive findings identify distinctive industrial structures and human figures as prominent objects of attention and suggest the value of coherent and person-centered narratives for content organization. These findings inform task-oriented functions, visual content selection, layered information presentation, and interaction flows, resulting in an augmented reality (AR) smart guide interface prototype. The study integrates findings on cultural identity and behavioral intention with visual attention and interview evidence to inform interaction design, providing an empirical basis for industrial heritage AR guides.
